question: Bind — ATK, 6-7, you are UP 4v3 after a Window pick, holding B Window on Bind with a rifle. The team is not yet committed to a site. How do you convert the 4v3?

options.label: Consolidate the man-advantage: group with your team and commit to ONE site with trade-spacing
options.explication_courte: A 4v3 is only worth something if you fight where the extra man can trade. Regrouping and hitting one site trade-spaced turns your lead into a series of favourable fights — you press the advantage without diluting it.

sources_option.citation: With a man advantage, commit together to one point trade-spaced so the extra man converts into traded duels

options.label: Hold B Window alone and wait to see where the 3 defenders rotate
options.explication_courte: Sitting on the info from Window is reasonable, but holding solo with a 4v3 lets the defense reset and play the clock. You have the advantage — passivity slowly gives it back rather than pressing it.

sources_option.citation: Info-holding is safe, but sitting on a numbers lead lets the defense reset and use the clock against you

options.label: Push B fast and alone through Window to press before they group
options.explication_courte: Solo-pushing B ahead of your team gives up the trade — if you die, your 4v3 collapses back to an even 3v3 and you've spent your advantage on one duel. Numbers advantages are pressed together, not alone.

sources_option.citation: Pushing ahead of your team while up hands the enemy an isolated duel and can erase the numbers lead

options.label: Split the 4 across A and B to double-threat both sites
options.explication_courte: Splitting a 4-man into two pairs versus 3 defenders wastes your extra man and lets them meet each half on even or favourable terms. Consolidate the lead; don't scatter it.

sources_option.citation: Splitting a grouped numbers advantage into smaller pieces lets the defense fight each half on better terms

explication_longue: Converting a mid-round numbers lead is where good teams win rounds they've already half-won. Up 6-7 in a 4v3 on Bind after picking a defender at Window, holding B Window with a rifle, the highest-EV line is to consolidate: regroup with your team and commit to ONE site with trade-spacing. A 4v3 is only worth something when you fight where the extra man can actually trade, so a grouped, spaced hit on a single site turns your lead into a run of favourable duels — you press the advantage without diluting it. Holding B Window alone to read the rotation is genuinely acceptable — the info has value — but sitting on a numbers lead lets the defense reset and burn the clock, slowly giving your edge back instead of pressing it. Solo-pushing B fast through Window is the costly error: peeling ahead of your team surrenders the trade, and if you die your 4v3 collapses to an even 3v3, your whole advantage spent on one duel. Splitting the four across A and B is the faute: two pairs versus three defenders wastes the extra man and lets them meet each half on even terms. Group up, space out, hit one site, and let the extra man do its job.

sources.citation: Convert a numbers lead by committing together to one point trade-spaced, not by holding passively, solo-pushing, or splitting
